name: Euro
seabedDepthNote: 45 m from the SOE dive calendar. Some dive reports give about 50 m.

pois.title: The Euro
pois.text: A steam tug, 130 by 22.5 by 12.2 feet. The register describes a screw steamer with one deck and a round stern, rigged as a fore-and-aft schooner. She worked for the Adelaide Steamship Company for most of her life, then for Howard Smith's Australian Steamships in Melbourne. Stripped and scuttled in the Ships' Graveyard outside Port Phillip Heads on 10 June 1948. She lies on her port side.
pois.photoCredit: Picture rendered from the SOE scan

pois.title: Boiler
pois.text: The boiler raised steam for the engine. Dive reports place it forward of the engine room.
pois.photoCredit: Picture rendered from the SOE scan

pois.title: Scuttling hole
pois.text: The Euro was sunk on 10 June 1948. Dive reports place the blast hole on the starboard side, between the engine and the boiler. The anchor on the main deck was not her own: it secured the tow rope for scuttling.
pois.photoCredit: Picture rendered from the SOE scan

pois.title: Engine room
pois.text: The Euro was driven by a single screw. Dive reports describe the triple-expansion steam engine, still in place.
pois.source: Dive reports (Aquability; The Scuba Doctor); Victorian Heritage Register, S247
pois.photoCredit: Picture rendered from the SOE scan

pois.title: Stern
pois.text: The register records a round stern. Dive reports note the steering quadrant here.
pois.source: Dive reports (Aquability; The Scuba Doctor); Victorian Heritage Register, S247
pois.photoCredit: Picture rendered from the SOE scan

pois.title: Wheelhouse
pois.text: An indicative wheelhouse of a steam tug of the 1890s: the master at the wheel, the binnacle with the magnetic compass and its correcting spheres, the engine room telegraph for orders to the engineer, the voice pipe to the engine room, and the chart table. To go inside, use Step into the wheelhouse in the panel, or swim in through the door. Not drawn from the Euro's plans.
pois.source: Indicative reconstruction, after tugs of the period

ghost.label: As built, indicative
ghost.note: Hull sized from the registered dimensions (130 x 22.5 x 12.2 ft) and fitted to the scan: she lies about 36 degrees to port, easing to about 30 degrees at the bow. The deck layout follows British-built steam tugs of the period: towing hook amidships abaft the funnel, a clear after deck under towing bows, steering quadrant on deck at the stern. Positions and sizes are indicative, not from the Euro's plans.
